Prolactin helps control the menstrual cycle and milk release, so a prolactinoma causes the amenorrhea-galactorrhea syndrome in women: milk from the breasts, which is galactorrhea, and, through negative feedback, a shutdown of the cycle, which is amenorrhea. They are usually microadenomas in premenopausal women. 2 Primary vs secondary lab patterns (TSH vs free T4; the same rule for ACTH) Flagged in the recording · 5 questions in the bank Know this Know the definitions, not just the patterns: secondary hyperthyroidism is a pituitary overproducing TSH. Primary hyperthyroidism: the thyroid overproduces T3 and T4 on its own, from a tumor or Graves disease, and the high hormone shuts off TSH by negative feedback. T4 high, TSH low. Nuclear pseudoinclusions: when the dip deepens until the membrane meets itself, a lobule of cytoplasm is trapped inside the nucleus. A groove comes before an inclusion. Grooves and inclusions are features of the BRAF mutation that defines papillary carcinoma. Psammoma bodies, in about 50 percent of cases. Papillae float on a small capillary and can die out; when they die, they calcify in laminated layers. When a true psammoma body is seen in the thyroid, papillary carcinoma is presumed. Graves disease is the most common cause of endogenous hyperthyroidism. It is autoimmune: an IgG autoantibody stimulates the TSH receptor, so the gland overproduces. The whole gland undergoes diffuse hyperplasia of its follicular cells, giving a goiter, and many patients have Graves ophthalmopathy. It is about 5 times more common in women. Hashimoto thyroiditis, properly called chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis, is a chronic autoimmune thyroiditis and the most common cause of hypothyroidism in the US. In this lecture, its antibodies are anti-TSH receptor antibodies that block the action of TSH, unlike the Graves autoantibodies, which stimulate the receptor. Same target, opposite effect. 6 Diabetes insipidus (central vs nephrogenic) vs SIADH (small cell lung carcinoma) Flagged in the recording · 3 questions in the bank Central diabetes insipidus is a deficiency of ADH. The patient has polyuria, a low urine specific gravity, and a high serum sodium and osmolality. The causes are head trauma, neoplasms, inflammatory disorders and surgery involving the pituitary or hypothalamus. 7 Pituitary adenomas: micro vs macro, mass effect, bitemporal hemianopsia, the functioning types Core of the slides · 4 questions in the bank A macroadenoma is greater than 10 millimeters. These come with local mass effect, often before any hormone symptoms: enlargement of the sella turcica, increased intracranial pressure, whose main symptoms are nausea and vomiting, headache and double vision. Because the optic chiasm sits right above the sella, a macroadenoma pushing upward can press on the chiasm or the optic nerves. Pressure on the chiasm hits its crossing central fibers and spares the uncrossed lateral fibers, so the outer half of each eye's field is lost: bitemporal hemianopsia, starting in the upper temporal quadrants. 8 Medullary carcinoma: C cells, RET and MEN 2, amyloid, calcitonin/chromogranin/CEA, sporadic vs familial Core of the slides · 3 questions in the bank Familial: younger patients, mean age 35; often multiple and bilateral; with associated C-cell hyperplasia; a component of MEN 2A and MEN 2B, through a germline RET mutation. Not RAS, not BRAF. Under the microscope it makes no thyroid hormone and no colloid. It looks like a neuroendocrine tumor: a solid, nested pattern of growth with a somewhat spindled quality. It also produces amyloid, which shows apple-green birefringence, and amyloid is a hint to the diagnosis. Immunohistochemistry confirms it: the tumor turns brown for calcitonin, its product, for chromogranin and synaptophysin, the neuroendocrine markers, and for CEA. 9 Hypopituitarism: the 75 percent rule, Sheehan syndrome, null cell adenoma, empty sella, and its symptoms Core of the slides · 5 questions in the bank Ischemic necrosis of the anterior pituitary, classically Sheehan syndrome: around delivery, a sudden drop in blood pressure stops the pituitary's blood supply, and the gland shuts down abruptly. Empty sella syndrome: an enlarged, empty sella turcica from chronic herniation of the subarachnoid space through a defect in the diaphragma sellae; the classic patients are obese, multiparous women. Dr. Dababneh said you don't need all of the details, only that the sella can turn up without its pituitary. The symptoms depend on which hormones are missing: fatigue, weight loss, decreased sex drive, sensitivity to cold, decreased appetite, facial puffiness, anemia and infertility. Women may have hot flashes, irregular or absent periods, loss of pubic hair and an inability to produce milk for breastfeeding. Men may have decreased facial or body hair. 10 Hypothyroid and hyperthyroid features: myxedema and cretinism (enlarged tongue), causes of hyperthyroidism Core of the slides · 3 questions in the bank The adult picture is called myxedema: apathy and mental sluggishness, weight gain, cold intolerance, lethargy, coarsening of the facial features, enlargement of the tongue and puffy hands, with puffiness from fluid in the legs and around the hands. The enlarged tongue and coarse face are findings a dentist may notice first. Dr. Dababneh admitted he wasn't sure why the tongue enlarges, "but that's what happens." An enlarged tongue in adult hypothyroidism, or myxedema, and in cretinism; coarse facial features in myxedema. 11 Thyroid development, follicular adenoma and anaplastic carcinoma Core of the slides · 4 questions in the bank The tumors above are well differentiated: they still look and stain like thyroid. Anaplastic, or undifferentiated, carcinoma has lost its differentiation; taken out of the neck, you couldn't tell where it came from. It is about 10 percent of thyroid cancers, at ages 60 to 80, often in areas of endemic goiter. It is a rapidly fatal neck mass that grows within a couple of months, invades the thyroid cartilage, the skin and the surrounding skeletal muscle, and metastasizes. It carries many mutations, such as p53. The biopsy shows high-grade nuclei and a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, resembling no particular tissue, and it may not even stain for thyroid markers. Also flagged in class Expect a lab-pattern question. Opposite directions (hormone vs TSH) = primary, the gland itself; same direction = secondary, the pituitary. Practice all four thyroid patterns and the same rule for ACTH and cortisol. He repeated the rule the next hour, so a corticotroph adenoma (Cushing disease) should read as ACTH high and cortisol high. Papillary = multifocal = total thyroidectomy; follicular = hemithyroidectomy is enough. BRAF = papillary, spreads by lymphatics to nodes; RAS = follicular, spreads by blood vessels to distant organs; RET = medullary. This is from the recording only. Papillary carcinoma nuclei are PALE, enlarged and overcrowded, with grooves and pseudoinclusions. A stem saying "hyperchromatic" is the trap. SIADH: low sodium, small cell lung cancer. DI is the opposite: high sodium, dilute urine. No ADH = polyuria (diabetes insipidus); too much ADH = water retention and hyponatremia (SIADH). The same trick works for the pituitary cells: the name says the hormone. Anaplastic carcinoma: rapidly fatal unless a targetable mutation (such as BRAF) is found. Follicular carcinoma spreads by blood; the slide names lung and bones (shoulder girdle, sternum, skull, iliac bones).
